A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Jamais Vu study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, tables and figures can be matched despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original correspondence evaluations on SPair-71k, SPair-U, AP-10K and PF-PASCAL, together with ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds loss-component comparisons, geometry sensitivity experiments and randomly sampled correspondence visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 refines the reported alignment procedure by explicitly constraining scale to s >= 1 to prevent collapse; v1 specifies only positive scale. The canonical prototype, principal losses, backbones and inference remain the same. Newly documented sampling and gradient details do not establish further changes to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use SPair-71k, SPair-U, AP-10K intra-species/cross-species/cross-family evaluations and PF-PASCAL. Random-point visualizations remain within the existing correspondence task. The newly stated 19,990 keypoint pairs clarify the retained SPair-U data rather than establish additional coverage.

E2.justification: The baseline rosters in Tables 1–3 and A2 are unchanged. New Table A1a expands the appendix comparison to sparse-only DINOv2+SD, Geo-SC losses, canonical-prototype losses without Geo-SC losses, and their combination.

E3.justification: New experiments compare loss combinations on SPair-71k test and SPair-U, sweep neighborhood sizes from 4 to 256, and test alignment using 3–8 selected keypoints versus all keypoints. Randomly sampled queries are also evaluated qualitatively. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B substantially expands beyond loss-weight and sampling-strategy checks to isolate canonical-prototype versus Geo-SC contributions and examine neighborhood size and global-versus-local alignment. Figures 5 and A4 add arbitrary-point matching case studies. The original ablation table survives as Table A1b; robust-metric results in Table A2 were already present.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, training seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its results. The added ablations continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–3, A2 and the original ablation rows are unchanged. New results include the canonical-prototype-only configuration's 75.9/66.0 PCK on SPair-71k/SPair-U, neighborhood and rigidity sensitivity scores, and random-point matching examples. These are additional configurations and observations, not improved scores for the retained model.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit nonshrinking scale constraint and explains the collapse degeneracy it addresses in the generalized Procrustes formulation. The displayed mathematical objectives are otherwise retained, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: exposing poor unseen-keypoint generalization, learning correspondence through a canonical geometric representation, and introducing SPair-U. Rewording and additional supporting experiments do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges that global rigid alignment is only a coarse approximation for deformable objects and explains its intended role. Appendix B adds interpretations attributing unseen-point generalization to canonical-prototype losses and seen-keypoint fitting to Geo-SC losses, alongside discussion of the new sensitivity results.

D1.justification: v2 substantially fills implementation gaps: it adds a project-repository link, 1,024-point farthest-point sampling, 64-point neighborhoods, pseudo-geodesic sampling pseudocode, and explicit blocking of geometric-loss gradients into P. Optimizer settings, hardware, runtime and the complete weighted loss were already documented in v1 and are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: Eight works are added, including TransforMatcher, warp-consistency methods, Diff3F and Umeyama's alignment algorithm. Section 2 also develops the distinction from SemAlign3D through inference cost, category requirements and segmentation requirements. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, introduction, method explanations and conclusion while preserving the overall section structure. It moves the complete loss and inherited Geo-SC details from Appendix A into Section 5.1, adds appendix subheadings, and clarifies terminology such as pseudo-geodesic sampling.

P2.justification: v2 adds matching visualizations in Figures 5 and A4 and Algorithm 1, and expands Table A1 into four panels. Figure 3 receives annotation-display cleanup and expanded statistics. Existing visual material is largely retained, including the canonical-shape figure renumbered from Figure 5 to Figure 6.

improvement.justification: The expanded component and geometry ablations strengthen support beyond v1's limited ablation study, while sampling pseudocode and optimization details reduce reproducibility gaps. The explicit rigidity limitation also improves interpretation. The overall gain is incremental: principal benchmark findings remain unchanged, and the new sensitivity studies use seen-keypoint validation results without uncertainty estimates.
